full_judgment:
This Rule was issued on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the defendant appellant-petitioner against the judgment and decree 18-4-1990 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge Naogaon in Title Appeal No. 121 of 1989 affirming those dated 13-4-1989 of the learned Assistant Judge, Naogaon in Other Class Suit No. 194 of 1988 decreeing the suit 

 6. The learned Assistant Judge, Naogaon tried the suit and on considering the materials and evidence on record decreed the suit. 

 7. The defendant-petitioner herein preferred Title Appeal No. 121 of 1980 in the court of the learned District Judge, Naogaon against the aforesaid judgment passed by the Assistant Judge, Naogaon. On transfer the learned Subordinate Judge, Naogaon heard the appeal and dismissed the same and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 14. On proper appreciation of the evidence on record the trial Court decreed the suit. The appellate Court below also rightly considered the evidences on record both oral and documentary and after proper discussion of evidence affirmed the judgment passed by the trial Court and held that the plaintiff is derived from being absorbed as teacher of the school while it was taken over by the Government and he had legal right to be absorbed as teacher of the said school. It appears from the judgments of both the courts below that the defendant No.8, the founder Chairman of the school, supported the plaintiff's case and the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 filed written statement supporting the case of the plaintiff' and the defendant Nos. 2, 5 and 6 also supported the case of the plaintiff in their cross-examination. Further, it appears from the attendance register which was exhibited before the trial Court as exhibit "Ka" that the defendant No. 1 was absent for long period but by erasing the relevant column he was allowed to put signature, which was done in collusion with the defendant No.2 to show that at the relevant time he was teacher of the said school. From the resolution book it appears that he was dismissed from service with effect from 11-2-1986 and, on the other hand, the plaintiff was appointed in his place with effect from 11-2-1986. 

 18. Mr. Halder, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, has referred to the case reported in 35 DLR 224 wherein a Single Bench of this court held that "A suit for declaration that the plaintiffs dismissal was illegal and not binding without asking for consequential relief for enforcing the declamatory decree. Omission to pray for consequential relief for enforcing declamatory decree renders it unenforceable in law". This decision was upheld by the Appellate Division in an unreported case being CPSLA No. 299 of 1983. On the other hand, a Division Bench of this court being presided over by his Lordships Mr. Justice Md. Ismailuddin Sarker held that "a suit for declaration that the order of removal of the plaintiff, a bank officer, from service, was void and inoperative and he remained in service, was maintainable without any prayer for further relief'. Both the reported cases were considered by his Lordships Mr. Justice Syed Amirul Islam in a judgment, reported in 49 DLR 38 wherein it has been held that in service matter a suit for simple declaration without any prayer for consequential relief is not maintainable. In this reported case various decisions of this sub- continent were considered and held that since the decision reported in 35 DLR 224 was affirmed by the Appellate Division in CPSLA No. 229 of 1983 (correct number is 299 of 1983) it was binding upon the High Court Division and, as such, the decisions reported in 45 DLR and 11 DLR were found conflicting with the proposition of law as laid down by the Appellate Division. 

 22. We may profitably refer to a case of Jibon Bima Corporation vs Mustafa Hussain and another reported in 50 DLR 411 wherein it has been held that "A declamatory decree passed in a case without any prayer for consequential relief is an annuity. Such declaration is a gain and its implementation is dependent on as to whom the decree is passed against. In the instant case the defendant being a statutory corporation, there is no reason to believe that such corporation will not implement the decision of the court. In this reported case various decisions including the decision reported in 35 DLR 224, 49 DLR 38, 1948 AIR (PC) 121, 52 CWN 761 (PC), PLD 1949 (Lahore) 219, 22 DLR 589, 45 DLR 375, 1995 BLD (AD) 239, 37 DLR 7, 11 DLR 528 and many other decisions were considered. It has been observed in the aforesaid decisions that while the Appellate Division in deciding the CPSLA No. 299 of 1983 it appears that the relevant decisions as stated above including 35 DLR 24 have not been placed before their Lordships for consideration. But their Lordships in the case reported in 45 DLR considered the aforesaid decisions and also the decision reported in 35 DLR 224 and then held that the suit for simple declaration is maintainable without any prayer for consequential relief
